Yes. Setting `alwaysApply: false` and tightening the description makes it agent-requested, so it only loads for algorithm/math work. Updating both the workspace and user copies.

---
description: >-
  Apply only when writing or refactoring algorithms, geometry, numerical
  methods, or other math-heavy code. Prefer readable, math-aligned names and
  structure over jargon and comment-heavy style.
alwaysApply: false
---

# Readable, Math-Aligned Code

When writing or refactoring code relating to an algorithm, optimize for a human reading it against the underlying math or design.

## Prefer code over comments

- Make names, helpers, and structure carry the meaning.
- Add a comment only when the code still cannot express intent (e.g. a non-obvious invariant or performance trick).
- Do not leave jargon parameters (`P`, `Q`, `subj`, `in`, `out`) unexplained - rename them instead.

## Match the math

- Extract named primitives that mirror the formulation (`cross`, `orient`, `lerp`) instead of inlining opaque expressions.
- Prefer small pure helpers; keep mutation localized (e.g. reusable buffers) when performance requires it.

## Descriptive names

- Name values by role in the algorithm (`current_polygon`, `cropping_polygon`), not by textbook shorthand or implementation accident.
- If a name needs a comment to be understood, rename it.

## Example

```
BAD:
  auto side = [&](auto& pt) { return ex * (pt[1] - ay) - ey * (pt[0] - ax); };

GOOD:
  // orient(a,b,p) = cross(b-a, p-a)
  inline double orient(const Vec2& a, const Vec2& b, const Vec2& p) {
      return cross(sub(b, a), sub(p, a));
  }
```

Yes. Updated both copies (workspace + user-level):

- `alwaysApply: false` - no longer injected into every chat
- Description rewritten so Cursor can pull it in only for algorithm / geometry / numerical / math-heavy work

It is now an **agent-requested** rule: the body stays out of context until the task looks relevant, which saves tokens on unrelated work.
